Animate Dead Animal.description: Gained at 6th level, this ability works like animate dead but is restricted to animal corpses and does not require any material component. It can be used once per day.

Blightfire.description: From 2nd level onward, as a standard action, the blighter can release a burst of searing flame. This deals 5d6 fire damage to every creature within a 10-foot radius (Reflex save for half; DC equals 10 + blighter class level + Wisdom modifier) and sets alight any flammable objects it contacts.

Contagious Touch.description: At 5th level, the blighter gains the ability to produce a contagious touch effect once per day. An additional daily use is gained for every two blighter levels beyond 5th.

Deforestation.description: Once per day as a full-round action, the blighter can slay all non-sentient plant life within a radius of 20 feet per class level. If an affected plant is controlled by another creature (for example, through a liveoak effect or as a dryad's bonded tree), the controller may attempt a Fortitude save (DC 10 + blighter level + Wisdom modifier) to protect it. Destroyed plants stop all biological functions immediately. They look healthy for a few hours but wilt and turn brown within a day. Except for plants saved by a controller, nothing can regrow in the blighted zone unless hallow is cast on the area and it is replanted. Performing deforestation is what empowers the blighter to cast her daily spells. This works in any terrain, but using it in an area with negligible vegetation (such as a barren desert or ice field) does not grant spellcasting ability.

Plague.description: At 10th level, the blighter can spread disease across a wide area. This works identically to contagious touch, except that it requires no attack roll and affects all designated targets within a 20-foot radius.

Speak With Dead Animal.description: Beginning at 4th level, the blighter can communicate with deceased animals. This works like speak with dead cast by a cleric whose level equals the sum of the character's druid and blighter levels, but it only applies to animal corpses. It can be used once per day.

Spells per Day.description: Because blighters are former druids, they forfeit their druid spellcasting. In its place, they gain a new and more destructive set of spells. At each blighter level, the character receives spell slots as shown in the class table, choosing from the blighter spell list. The blighter's caster level equals the sum of her blighter and druid levels. Casting a blighter spell requires a Wisdom score of at least 10 + the spell's level; a blighter with Wisdom 10 or lower cannot cast these spells. Bonus spells are determined by Wisdom, and spell save DCs equal 10 + spell level + Wisdom modifier. When the class table shows 0 spells per day for a given level, the blighter receives only whatever bonus spells her Wisdom score provides at that level. The blighter has access to the entire blighter spell list and may freely select which spells to prepare, just as a druid does (though spontaneous casting of summon spells is not available). Spell preparation and casting follow the same procedure as a druid. The blighter fuels her daily spellcasting through deforestation; if more than 24 hours pass without deforesting a wooded area, she loses the ability to cast spells until she does so again. The standard divine focus for blighter spells is a dried sprig of holly or mistletoe, and any material component must have been dead for at least one day before use.

Sustenance.description: From 2nd level onward, the blighter no longer requires food or water to survive.

Unbond.description: Starting at 8th level, the blighter can temporarily sever the bond between a creature and its bonded animal or magical beast (such as a companion, familiar, or special mount) once per day. The bonded creature must be within 40 feet of both its master and the blighter. If the master fails a Will save (DC 10 + blighter level + Wisdom modifier), the bond is broken as though the servitor had perished, though a familiar's loss does not cost experience points. Creatures that are ordinarily hostile will turn on their former masters but are not otherwise affected. The bond restores itself after 1 minute per blighter level, returning all associated benefits. The master may also reclaim the servitor through the usual means of acquiring one.

Undead Wild Shape.description: At 3rd level, the blighter gains a specialized form of wild shape. This functions like the druid's wild shape ability, except the blighter applies the skeleton template to the chosen animal form. The skeletal animal form has the following modifications: its type becomes undead; natural armor bonus is +0 (Tiny), +1 (Small), +2 (Medium or Large), or +3 (Huge); it gains +2 Dexterity and has no Constitution score; it is immune to cold; and it has damage reduction 5/bludgeoning. The blighter receives one additional daily use of this ability at every even-numbered blighter level after 3rd. At 5th level, the blighter can assume the form of a Large skeletal animal, and at 9th level, a Huge skeletal animal becomes available.

Weapon and Armor Proficiency.description: This class does not provide any additional weapon or armor proficiencies.
